title: Four English and Scottish moth samples gave no clear common decline in warmth slopes from 8 to 16 C in 1993-2015
abstract: We tested whether moth catch had a smaller warmth slope on warm nights than on cool nights. Conditional Poisson models used 27,881 nights in England and Scotland in 1993-2003 and 2004-2015. They controlled trap-week totals and other night weather. Three estimates of the slope at 16 C minus the slope at 8 C were negative. Later Scotland gave a positive estimate. All four year-cluster intervals included zero after four-test correction. Summer-only estimates were all negative, but only later England had a corrected interval below zero. This exploratory follow-up reuses a published panel. It does not establish a linear response or separate flight activity from abundance. Few Scottish sites, sparse warm nights, source preprocessing and short-term emergence limit inference. The package gives original code, aggregate model evidence, hashes and retrieval instructions. It tests no air pollution effect.

display.caption: Local log catch slopes at 8 and 16 C and their direct difference. Bars give year-cluster intervals with correction for four tests.

citations.reason: Reuses the verified published night panel. Adds a curvature contrast with independent estimator code and year clusters. Biological observations overlap.
